transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-30 16:00 PT | Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording) | Note: partial auto-join artifacts
Attendees: Liam Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Evan Park (CTO - Asterion Labs), Sofia Martinez (Head of ML Platform - Asterion), Jordan Lee (Cloud Ops)

Summary:
- Quarterly health check focused on usage growth, cost trajectory, reliability incidents, and pilot ramp for private/dedicated capacity.
- Customer leaning toward a Dedicated pilot but wants cost/regression checks and SOC2 + KMS detail for VPC deployment.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing, run benchmarks on representative prompt set, and propose rollout timeline.

Topics covered:
1) Recent usage: burst patterns and tail latency
2) Cost per 1k tokens under current config and optimization levers (batching, quantize)
3) Reliability: 2 small incidents in April (cold-starts during burst) and mitigation plan
4) Pilot scope: Dedicated GPU pool vs Private VPC, canary rollout, data residency concerns
5) Security checklist: SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration, audit logs retention

Action items (short): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam Ortega: alright, thanks everyone for joining, um this is the Q2 signal review for Asterion, I see all the usual suspects, Evan, Sofia, Jordan, hey, can you hear me ok?
[00:07] Dr. Evan Park: yeah good, we can hear you, thanks Liam.
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: yep all set.
[00:12] Liam Ortega: cool. quick agenda, we'll run usage and cost, then Priya will do a quick perf and optimization playback, then we talk security and pilot scope and close with next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Jordan Lee: yep that's fine.
[00:25] Liam Ortega: okay, starting with usage. so we've seen steady growth—about 2.8x month over month from January to May, bursts around product launch last week, peak qps ~1.6k for about 20 minutes. Evan, can you confirm those burst windows?
[00:38] Dr. Evan Park: yeah the push last Wednesday was the traffic spike, that came from our new recommendation widget; sessions are longer now too which adds to token counts. we also noticed a lot of retrys from the mobile client at p95.
[00:50] Sofia Martinez: correct, mobile has some flaky network conditions, multiple small retries which inflated token usage. we are working on backoff.
[00:58] Liam Ortega: ok makes sense. Priya, you had a cost model?
[01:02] Priya Nair: yeah, I put together two quick buckets — hosted baseline and dedicated pilot estimate. Hosted at current gen model and their prompt mix sits around $0.29 per 1k tokens effective after our discounting assumptions; with current burst pattern that projects to about $18k this month. Dedicated pilot assumptions, with 2x A100-equivalent nodes and persistent pools, amortized run rate looks closer to $9k-$12k depending on utilization and whether you leverage quantization. caveat, these are roughs — we need the exact token mix.
[01:30] Dr. Evan Park: that hosted number seems higher than our spreadsheet, did you include the KV cache hit rates? we have a local prefix cache that handles about 20% of traffic.
[01:40] Priya Nair: good point, Evan. I used conservative cache hit 10% for the customer-level mix. If you can confirm 20% that drops hosted bill by roughly 8-10%. also batching and async retries play big roles.
[01:53] Jordan Lee: our infra team hasn't pushed caching metrics to the reporting bucket yet but we'll export that.
[01:57] Sofia Martinez: noted, Jordan will follow up.
[02:00] Liam Ortega: perfect. quick thread on reliability — April had two short incidents, one was an autoscaler misfire that led to a backlog and higher latencies, the other was a cold-start on a seldom-used GPU pool. Priya — what mitigations does Redwood recommend?
[02:15] Priya Nair: several things — 1) more aggressive warm pools for tail events, 2) a small hot standby for critical routes, 3) KV caching prefilling for common prefixes, 4) better queueing/backpressure at gateway. we can also tune autoscaler windows and cooldowns. note: warm pools increase baseline cost but reduce p99 spikes.
[02:35] Dr. Evan Park: tradeoff is acceptable if it prevents customer-facing timeouts. what's the expected delta in cost for warm pools?
[02:42] Priya Nair: ballpark 7-12% on the committed capacity run rate for the hot-standby + warmed nodes. again depends on how many routes you mark critical.
[02:50] Jordan Lee: for us, only the recommendation API needs the p99 SLA; other routes can tolerate a few 100s ms.
[02:56] Liam Ortega: good call. now on security/ops: Evan asked about VPC private deployment vs Redwood dedicated. Evan, what's top priority?
[03:05] Dr. Evan Park: data residency and KMS integration — we need customer-managed keys and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also, SOC2 report is required for our vendors.
[03:16] Liam Ortega: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we can forward audit logs; I'll send the SOC2 package. Priya, any notes on the private package?
[03:24] Priya Nair: yes, Private control plane option gives you full VPC peering and HSM/KMS integration; the on-prem package is heavier. For the pilot we typically run VPC mode with dedicated GPU pool in the region. There are some network egress considerations.
[03:37] Sofia Martinez: we need egress patterns documented; finance wants worst-case monthly.
[03:41] Liam Ortega: we'll include an egress estimate in the pricing pack.
[03:45] Dr. Evan Park: also SSO — we use Okta SAML, want RBAC mapped to groups.
[03:50] Priya Nair: SAML/SSO is supported; we can map groups to roles in the console. we also have audit log retention options (30/90/365 days) as an add-on.
[03:59] Jordan Lee: cool.
[04:02] Liam Ortega: moving on to pilot scope. Priya, can you outline the recommended pilot plan?
[04:07] Priya Nair: sure — pilot premise: 4 week validation window, two dedicated GPU nodes (hot + warm), canary on 10% traffic for week 2, full cutover if performance & quality pass. deliverables: perf report, cost projection, regression evals on your prompt set, runbook for failover to hosted model.
[04:25] Dr. Evan Park: 4 weeks feels short if we need data residency proofs. can we extend to 6 weeks?
[04:29] Priya Nair: yes, 6 weeks is reasonable — we can structure milestones at week 2, week 4 and week 6 for canaries and final signoff.
[04:37] Sofia Martinez: for signoff we want two things: latency band adherence (p95 < 250ms for recommendation endpoint) and no regression on answer quality measured by our eval suite.
[04:47] Priya Nair: understoood — we can integrate an eval harness and run A/B comparisons. note that quantized models can slightly shift generation distributions; we'll include regression thresholds.
[04:58] Liam Ortega: quick interruption — Jordan, can you remind us of the procurement timeline? do you need an SOW for legal review?
[05:05] Jordan Lee: procurement wants SOW + SAAS agreement, plus SOC2 and DPAs. Timeline wise, procurement meeting earliest 2027-06-10; legal usually takes 2 weeks.
[05:14] Liam Ortega: ok we'll aim to have docs to you by June 3.
[05:18] Dr. Evan Park: on performance, Priya, can you run an estimate for cold-start p95? we saw 1-2s tail during the incident.
[05:25] Priya Nair: cold-starts vary with model and KV cache; with warmed standby we see p95 drop to ~200-350ms for the rec endpoint. cold GPU allocation can be 600-1,200ms depending on autoscaler.
[05:36] Sofia Martinez: that matches what we measured, sometimes up to 1.5s, which causes mobile timeouts.
[05:41] Liam Ortega: noted. next, conversation about cost levers. Priya — you mentioned quantization; if we run 4-bit quantized instances what quality impact?
[05:49] Priya Nair: 4-bit sometimes has slight token-level variance — in our evals for the open model family you saw 1-2% drop on scored NLI tasks, for retrieval-augmented generation majority of user-visible metrics are stable but we will validate on your prompts. cost reductions can be 30-45% per-token compute cost.
[06:08] Dr. Evan Park: we need that validation before committing. can Redwood flag any hallucination regressions automatically?
[06:14] Priya Nair: we have a quality monitoring feature that ties to prompt-sets and will alert on metric drift; we can surface diffs and example pairs.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: perfect. legal question — is there data residency support for EU-only? our EU customers must not cross borders.
[06:29] Liam Ortega: yes, we can pin region in Dedicated & Private; hosted may have multi-region failover unless pinned. we'll document region pinning in the SOW.
[06:37] Sofia Martinez: thanks.
[06:39] Liam Ortega: there's been mention of competitors — Evan, you said engineering ran an A/B with a vendor trial?
[06:45] Dr. Evan Park: yes, they ran a short proof against OpenAI and an internal layer; OpenAI was good for dev but cost was again high at scale; in-house layer had reliability issues.
[06:55] Priya Nair: that's consistent; vendors are getting close on quality but serving economics and network ownership become big differentiators.
[07:02] Liam Ortega: okay, let's talk timeline recap. target pilot start: 2027-06-14 (assuming docs signed by 2027-06-10). milestone map: week 1 config & baseline, week 2 canary 10%, week 4 performance rubric, week 6 final signoff.
[07:16] Jordan Lee: procurement could push a week; we put a soft buffer of 1 week.
[07:20] Dr. Evan Park: understood.
[07:22] Sofia Martinez: small note — we will provide a sample prompt corpus. some prompts contain PHI redacted — legal approved redaction but we want to confirm telemetry sanitization.
[07:33] Priya Nair: Redwood supports PII/PHI masking for telemetry; we'll show the config.
[07:38] Liam Ortega: awesome. any other open questions?
[07:41] Jordan Lee: only one: if we choose dedicated vs private later, what's migration complexity?
[07:47] Priya Nair: migration path is standard — models and routing policies are portable; Private adds VPC peering and KMS wiring which is mainly network and key rotation work. we keep the same API layer so app changes are minimal.
[07:59] Dr. Evan Park: great.
[08:01] Liam Ortega: alright let's do a quick readout of action owners — I'll go first. Liam to send SOC2 + private deployment pack and draft SOW by 2027-06-03. Priya to prepare perf config + batching/quantization proposal and runbook by 2027-06-02. Jordan to export cache hit & p95 latency traces and procurement timeline by 2027-06-04. Asterion to share prompt corpus and traffic histogram by 2027-06-04.
[08:27] Sofia Martinez: sounds good.
[08:29] Dr. Evan Park: thanks everyone.
[08:31] Liam Ortega: thanks, we'll follow up via email and sync calendar for the perf run.
[08:36] (recording stops)

Recap (auto):
- Pilot agreed in principle: 6-week option preferred.
- Key success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms for critical endpoint, no regression on eval suite, SOC2 + KMS integration validated.
- Risks: cache instrumentation gaps, procurement timing, slight quality delta with aggressive quantization.
